title: Blond Braids In A Chinese Desert Grave Baffled Everyone

segments.narration: Blond braids survived four thousand years in a desert grave. The Taklamakan in western China is dry enough to keep hair and skin.
Hundreds of bodies, buried from about 2100 BC, dressed in woollen clothes, felt caps and leather boots. The hair ran red, brown and blond.
For decades the obvious answer was migration from the west: European-speaking herders pushing east across the steppe. But whose bodies were these really?
In 2021 a genome study read thirteen of them. No western steppe ancestry at all. Seventy-two percent Ancient North Eurasian.
They were a local population, genetically isolated, who borrowed herding and farming from their neighbours. The faces were never foreign. Only the ideas were.

verdicts.claim: Bronze Age mummies from the Tarim Basin in Xinjiang, China, preserved hair ranging from blond to red to deep brown, generally long, curly and braided.
verdicts.note: 100% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article

verdicts.claim: The earliest Tarim Basin burials date to roughly 2135-1939 BCE and the bodies were buried in woollen garments, felt caps and leather boots.
verdicts.note: 100% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 2 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The mummies were previously argued to be Proto-Tocharian-speaking pastoralists descended from the Afanasievo culture or from populations of the Bactria-Margiana complex, that is, migrants from further west.
verdicts.note: 73% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article

verdicts.claim: A 2021 Nature study by Zhang and colleagues sequenced 13 Early Bronze Age Tarim individuals dated 2135-1623 BCE and found about 72% Ancient North Eurasian ancestry with about 28% Ancient Northeast Asian and no detectable Western Steppe ancestry.
verdicts.note: Both the Nature paper and Wikipedia give the 13 individuals, the 2135-1623 BCE range, the ~72%/28% split and the absence of Western Steppe ancestry.

verdicts.claim: The study concluded they were a genetically isolated local population that adopted neighbouring pastoralist and agriculturalist practices rather than descending from migrants.
verdicts.note: 88% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article
